verdicts.trueWording: can rely on her explaining that difference in due course
verdicts.note: Exact on the live page (HTTP 200, raw HTML). Full sentence: 'You know that there's something different in what she's describing and can rely on her explaining that difference in due course.' The 'rather than at once' limb is carried by the next sentence, 'But first, there's our curiosity to be fed.'

verdicts.trueWording: It was built of uncut rocks roughly mortared
verdicts.note: Exact inside Tomlinson's block quotation of the novel's page-1 opening, introduced as 'start on page 1 by describing the wall'. Tomlinson's text has a colon after 'mortared' where other editions print a full stop; the quoted limb itself is verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: In just a few pages of dense, carefully-worked text
verdicts.note: Exact; full sentence continues 'Le Guin depicts the under-belly of an otherwise dazzling society.' Every limb of the claim is on the page (claim drops only the word 'otherwise').

verdicts.trueWording: Street lights were broken, windows shuttered, shop fronts gutted by fire
verdicts.note: Exact. The 'poor quarter of Nio' limb is supported by the preceding sentences: Shevek escapes 'into the Old Town of Urras's main city Nio. There he finds poverty that had been kept hidden from him.'

verdicts.trueWording: we swoop down over the island, from its high peak
verdicts.note: Quotation is exact, but Goss never frames the movement as a camera. Her figure is the reader in motion under a bird's-eye view: 'often called a bird's eye view', 'At the beginning of Le Guin's book, we are the Sparrowhawk. We move as the hawk moves.' The hawk figure is load-bearing for her (it ties the viewpoint to Sparrowhawk), so 'camera' is the claimant's metaphor, not Goss's.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the 'camera' figure - Goss says bird's eye view and 'we move as the hawk moves', never a camera

verdicts.trueWording: The opening moves from a grander, larger view toward a smaller, more intimate one
verdicts.note: Exact; the sentence continues ': Sparrowhawk to Ged to Duny.' All limbs supported.

Exact, and its 'descending order' limb is supplied by the same sentence ('moves from a grander, larger view toward a smaller, more intimate one') and the parallel list following it, 'Dragonlord to archmage to goat herd.' The three names are one subject.

verdicts.trueWording: This entire scene is structured by the oppositions between boy and man, village and world
verdicts.note: Exact. The page's list continues 'present and future', and adds 'the opposition between poetry and prose'; the claim quotes a subset, which is not a contradiction.

verdicts.trueWording: No people appear in the first paragraph
verdicts.note: Exact on the live page. Merrill's sentence continues that people are alluded to on the second page and no specific characters appear until the third.

verdicts.trueWording: no names are mentioned until the seventh
verdicts.note: Exact; the governing unit is pages, set by the same sentence's 'on the book's second page' and 'until the third'. Merrill's own text later calls Shevek 'the first named character in the book'.

verdicts.trueWording: the rough and improvised nature of a key setting
verdicts.note: Exact. It is one item in Merrill's list of what is 'already laid out for readers in the novel's opening paragraph', which supports the 'establishes' limb; the page adds 'even after seven generations of settlement'.

verdicts.trueWording: things that do not look important but are
verdicts.note: Exact, and it is the first item in that same opening-paragraph list, so the 'lists among the opening paragraph's subjects' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: hint at the full lives they have lived off the page
verdicts.note: Exact; full sentence: 'Le Guin's sketches of incidental characters hint at the full lives they have lived off the page.'

verdicts.trueWording: Her writing is spare and lyrical, just begging to be read aloud
verdicts.note: Exact. Byline and date on the page match the citation: 'February 13, 2014 by alannaofdoom'; the site header now reads Cannonball Read 18, the review is tagged #CBR6.

verdicts.trueWording: From the very first lines, it has the feel of an old legend, told and retold around hearth fires
verdicts.note: Exact through 'hearth' and beyond ('hearth fires for generations'). It immediately follows the 358 sentence, matching the cited 'second point' location.
